title: The Mixtape of the quarry
premise: Sebastian Zhou has spent seventeen years perfecting the art of invisibility, kneading his unspoken feelings into sourdough while the students of Quarry High chase glory. But when the school's legendary ghost — a swimmer who drowned in the quarry decades ago — begins leaving notes addressed to him in ink that shifts like water, Sebastian learns the ghost is bound to a bargain: every generation, someone must win both the state championship and the school's secret, unwinnable contest of truths, or the ghost claims a life. As Sebastian uncovers that the town's founding families built their power on the original drowning, he must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy his best friend's family and paying the price of silence. In the end, Sebastian wins neither championship but breaks the bargain itself by baking the ghost's true story into bread and feeding it to the whole town, freeing them both at the cost of the bakery and his own clean record.
about_author: Juniper Marchetti is the pen name of a former line cook who grew up above her family's bakery in a rust-belt quarry town, where local legends were served alongside the morning rolls. She writes young adult stories about quiet kids who discover that small towns keep their secrets the way ovens keep heat.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. During championship season, Sebastian finds a note in his locker reading 'You bake what you won't say' in ink that ripples like pond water. He dismisses it until the same impossible ink appears on his proofing cloth. When he tests the legend by answering aloud in the empty pool room, the reply comes instantly: 'I know your name, Sebastian Zhou.' The beat is dread laced with a terrible thrill of being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with the ghost, Wren Calloway, 1974. Wren reveals she didn't drown accidentally — the founding families sacrificed her to seal a bargain that keeps the quarry profitable and the school untouchable, and each generation must renew it through two victories. Meanwhile Sebastian's best friend Dev's father, a founding heir, grows suspicious of Sebastian's questions. The emotional beat is the seduction of forbidden knowledge and the first crack in loyalty.

chapters.title: Two Championships
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The secret contest of truths begins: anonymous accusations posted school-wide, each one a test of whether students will trade honesty for safety. Sebastian realizes winning means denouncing Dev's family — and losing means Wren takes someone. At the state meet, Dev throws his race to protect his father, and Sebastian must choose whether to win alone. The beat is betrayal compounding betrayal as survival starts to look like corruption.

chapters.title: The Recipe
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Sebastian loses the truth contest deliberately, and as the bargain turns toward Dev, he bakes Wren's full story — names, dates, the founding families' signatures — into hundreds of loaves for the championship celebration. The town eats the truth; the bargain, built on secrecy, dissolves. Wren fades free, Dev forgives him slowly, and Sebastian reopens the bakery under new ownership. The beat is grief transmuted into release: some prices can be paid together instead of alone.
